what_i_did: make_views.py cuts the 9 pieces out of mj/ground-cover/sheet.png into views/<piece>.png and keys a mask for each. The cast shadows are a pale green, so a pixel is dropped as shadow when it is light and blue-ish: B/G above 0.70 and mean between 0.55 and 0.80. The upper bound keeps the cream clover heads.

score.py renders each GLB with the harness lens (50 mm, 1.9 x the bbox diagonal), front-on and 16 deg up, and scores the silhouette IoU with harness.norm_mask. A sweep over 6 to 24 deg moved the tufts by under 0.03. Only the path edge clearly preferred a higher camera, so I kept 16.

Each tuft has 4 rings of blades rooted on small circles on the ground (8, 10, 11 and 11 blades). Each blade is a 3-triangle strap with a blunt round end: two strap triangles from its ring segment, plus one wide-angle cap. Inner rings stand at 16 to 22 deg and reach the full height. Outer rings splay to 70 to 80 deg and are shorter, so each tuft is a broad dome with 40 blades in 120 triangles. Each blade bows outward and has its own small shade shift. tuft-f (wispy) uses the same build with blades a quarter as wide and tighter rings.

The normals are authored. Each vertex uses a dome normal from a point half a tuft below the ground, blended 50/50 with up. Every triangle is wound so its front agrees with that normal. The material is double-sided, and the side facing out and up is always the front, so three.js's back-face normal flip only lands on the undersides and on the inside of the far blades, which should be in shade anyway. I tried single-sided crowns. They scored higher (about 0.60 mean), but from 45 deg they showed only the far half of each tuft, a fan instead of a rosette, so I dropped them (r/kit_45.png shows the final from 45 deg).

COLOR_0 is a vertex colour that the material's base colour reads directly. Blades go from a dark base (foliage #6e9440 mixed 30 % toward meadow, at 78 % brightness) to a light tip. The tip is meadow #a6b087 drifted toward foliage by a per-tuft amount: a 0.55, b 0.70, c 0.30, d 0.60, e 0.45, f 0.25. Inner rings are a few percent lighter.

Every mesh carries a float vertex attribute `_sway`: 0 at the root and 1 at the tip of every blade, stem and leaf, 1.0 on the flower and clover heads (they ride their stem tips), and 0 on the moss and pebbles. Blender's glTF exporter writes it as the custom attribute `_SWAY` (export_attributes=True). three.js GLTFLoader loads it as geometry.attributes._sway. COLOR_0 alpha is left at 1.

22 trefoils. Each has three 3-triangle rounded leaflets on a low elliptical mound, laid in a golden-angle spiral, over a flat 24-triangle core dome so the patch reads as one mat. There are 7 white heads, each an 8-triangle squashed octahedron, on 2-triangle stems. Materials: Clover_Leaf and Flower_White.

16 two-segment stems (Grass_Stem) carry 20 five-petal cup flowers, 70 % yellow (Flower_Yellow) and 30 % lilac (Flower_Lilac); 4 of the flowers sit on side twigs. The leafy base is 3 small rings of narrow strap leaves (Grass_Leaf), the same build as the tufts.

A lumpy elliptical moss berm (Moss_Path, 12 x 4 rings, two soft humps) with a dirt-tinted rim on the front (-Y, path) side. 4 half-buried pebbles (Stone_Pebble, 15 triangles each) sit along the front edge, and 5 small round-tipped blades (Grass_Meadow) stand on top. The moss and pebbles are single-sided closed shapes, and their sway is 0.
good: Every piece is within budget: each tuft 120/120, clover 292/300, wildflowers 265/300, path edge 179/200.
No spikes: every blade ends in a blunt round cap, and from above (r/kit_45.png) the tufts read as soft full rosettes with no hole in the middle.
The vertex colour runs from a dark base to a light tip. Normals are smooth and authored, so there are no flat facets and no blades turned black by a back face.
The `_sway` attribute exports as a real glTF custom attribute, so nothing has to be packed into the colour alpha.
off: The tufts are sparser and spikier in outline than the sheet's dense painted domes. The sheet has about 60 overlapping paddles a tuft; 120 triangles buys 40 thin straps with gaps between them. The IoU loss (0.49 to 0.60) is mostly that see-through fill, not the outline.
The blade ends are blunt (a wide-angle 1-triangle cap), not fully round. The 2-triangle round cap I tried cost a quarter of the blades.
tuft-f scores lowest (0.35): its painted blades are long, curving and overlapping, while these are straight thin straps.
The clover heads are faceted white bipyramids, not fluffy balls, and the patch has fewer, larger leaves than the sheet.
The wildflower clump is airier than the sheet's bush of stems (IoU 0.40).
The path edge's moss is smoother and lighter than the sheet's textured olive moss, and its pebbles are smaller and fewer.

rounds.change: 17 curved 7-triangle ribbons a tuft, roots on a disc, double-sided with outward winding. Read as sparse agave rosettes.
Hemisphere (cos-uniform) blade fan plus a faceted 8-sided core dome; bigger clover leaves plus a core; wildflower leafy base.
29 cheaper 4-triangle paddles a tuft, no core. Denser, but the double-sided normal flip turned half the blades dark.
Single-sided scalloped cone crowns (front = inside). Best IoU and dense, but from 45 deg only the far half of each tuft showed.

Ring-rooted 3-triangle straps (40 a tuft), double-sided, each triangle wound to agree with its authored dome normal. Dome tilt and length profile tuned; darker moss, rounder clover heads. Final: 768 px, 48 samples.

moving_parts: None baked in. Wind is the game's: bend each vertex by _sway (0 root .. 1 tip) times the weather signal's wind.
creative_additions: Each tuft drifts by its own amount between meadow and foliage, so the 6 tufts can mix in the meadow without a visible repeat. The path edge has a dirt-tinted rim on its path side.
